Daniel / Maria —

We detected a sustained increase in 95th percentile inference latency impacting requests routed to the aurora model variant in us-west (started ~07:58 PST). We have opened an incident bridge and assembled engineering: Grace O'Connor (runtime), Rachel Kim (SRE), and I are on the call now.

What we know so far (08:21 PST):
- Scope: Elevated tail latency for /v1/generate affecting a subset of high-concurrency customers, Aurora observing increased response times.
- Current impact: Increased response latency; error rate remains within tolerance. No evidence of data loss.
- Root cause (initial): High KV cache turnover and suboptimal kernel selection under the current batch/seq-length mix.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Grace is forcing a conservative kernel selection and increasing memory reservation on the affected GPU pool.
- Rachel is isolating high-concurrency client sessions and applying a temporary routing rule to rebalance load across spare dedicated nodes.
- We are enabling prefix caching for Aurora tenant to reduce repeated context recomputation (will take ~10-15 minutes to seed).

Estimated next update: 08:45 PST (we will provide an interim exec summary then).
